text:
Priya Sharma: FYI incoming escalation from Acme about onboarding -> started seeing a big uptick in 429s right after the rate-limit policy push this morning. They reported ~30% of requests failing with 429s.

Ethan Cole: thanks priya. do we have the policy id that rolled?

Priya Sharma: policy id `rl-policy-2026-03-12-v2` — Lina pushed it during the 08:15 deploy window. customer first noticed errors ~08:30.

Lina Gomez: yea that was the canary push (10% of infra). the change tightened per-user burst from 120->30 in a 60s window to reduce token usage. it passed unit tests and local load, but looks like Acme has very bursty auth flows.

Marcus Yu: billing note — Acme also flagged unexpected billing spikes coincident with retries; they retried aggressively client-side. they sent sample headers: `x-rate-limit-limit: 30`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 24`

Priya Sharma: they included a curl repro. can reproduce 429s locally: 
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %url_effective\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME-TOKEN>" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/engines/gen:default/completions; done
```
rapid bursts >30 req/min -> 429.

Ethan Cole: can you paste the request-ids? need to pull from gateways/traces.

Priya Sharma: sample: `req=01G1X4Z9A2KJ3X0R1Q`, `req=01G1X5A0B5LJ4Y1Z2P`. attached logs show `quota_exhausted: burst_window` errors in the ingress logs.

ops-bot: Deploy event: `rl-policy-2026-03-12-v2` rolled to canary group (10% traffic) at 2026-03-12T08:15:03Z.

Lina Gomez: quick analysis: our canary weighted to specific regions; looks like Acme traffic mapped to that canary slice. two issues: (1) reduction of burst size was aggressive; (2) our `x-rate-limit-remaining` header is opaque when use of pooled API keys occurs (Acme uses rotating tokens).

Ethan Cole: proposal: (A) roll back canary to previous policy immediately for that slice, (B) add a short soft-penalty mode for tokens with rotating patterns (grace credits), (C) follow up to change policy to 60->45 burst for a week. which do you prefer for immediate mitigation?

Priya Sharma: Acme wants errors stopped now. they can tolerate a short rollback. can we do (A) + (B) short term?

Lina Gomez: I can rollback the canary slice in ~4 minutes. to implement soft-penalty requires code change to the token-bucket refiller — not safe for immediate. but we can enable a per-customer override for Acme in config. that is quick.

Ethan Cole: ok Lina — roll back the canary slice and enable per-customer override for Acme (override increases burst window back to 120) for now. keep me posted.

Lina Gomez: starting rollback now. command: `./infractl rollout cancel rl-policy-2026-03-12-v2 --scope canary-10pct`

ops-bot: Rollout action initiated by Lina Gomez at 2026-03-12T08:46:11Z.

Priya Sharma: pinging Acme with timeline, asking them to throttle retries and to include `Retry-After` handling. will also ask for sample SDK version. :thumbsup:

Marcus Yu: putting a temporary billing credit on their account for the retry storm. note: recommend we also add a header `x-quota-suggested-backoff` in future to help SDKs.

Ethan Cole: after rollback completes we should run a quick synthetic test: 2 clients, one steady 20rps and one bursty 100rps for 30s and check SLA. Priya, can you coordinate with Acme to run that?

Priya Sharma: yes, scheduled a short window with them at 09:15. I asked them to use the minimal repro script and to send request-ids.

Lina Gomez: rollback finished. ops-bot shows `rl-policy-2026-03-12-v1` active for that slice now.

ops-bot: Rollout complete: `rl-policy-2026-03-12-v2` removed from canary-10pct at 2026-03-12T08:50:02Z.

Ethan Cole: good. Marcus, please confirm billing credit applied and any alerts suppressed for Acme during the window.

Marcus Yu: credit applied. suppressed noisy alerts for Acme from 08:30-09:00. added a follow-up ticket on billing analytics to flag retry-driven cost spikes. ticket: INF-4622.

Priya Sharma: Acme ran the synthetic at 09:15. they still see some 429s at the >100rps bursts but overall much improved. they attached request-ids — I grabbed traces.

Ethan Cole: trace shows token-bucket refill was at 0 after sustained bursts; our KV-cache of client fingerprinting mis-attributed some rotating tokens to the same bucket, then reset. That explains the higher-than-expected rejections.

Lina Gomez: action items: 
- revert the permanent policy change, leave v1 as baseline (done)
- implement per-customer overrides in config (short term)
- create follow-up PR to improve token-fingerprinting for rotating keys (refactor KV keying)
- add `x-quota-suggested-backoff` + better headers for SDK guidance
- add canary coverage test to include bursty clients

Priya Sharma: putting this in a customer post-mortem and pinging Acme with mitigation summary + ask for SDK versions. thanks team.

Ethan Cole: thanks all. we'll schedule a postmortem to decide safe policy defaults and rollout process updates. please add notes to INF-4623 (canary rollout playbook).

Marcus Yu: FYI for PMs — we should coordinate billing notifications when rate policy changes that are expected to increase client retries.

Priya Sharma: closing loop with Acme; if anything else shows up I'll reopen. :white_check_mark:

Lina Gomez: leaving this thread open for final doc updates.

ops-bot: Thread archived automatically after inactivity.
